# Categorized releases page

The Nextor repository publishes each component (kernel base, standalone drivers, NEXTOR.SYS, COMMAND3.COM, the tools, mknexrom...) as a separate GitHub release, which makes the flat releases list hard to navigate. The page in `docs/releases`, generated with [github-categorized-releases](https://github.com/Konamiman/github-categorized-releases), groups the releases by component. It is kept in source control and served by GitHub Pages, together with the rest of the documentation, from the `docs` directory: https://konamiman.github.io/Nextor/releases/

Files in this directory:

- `config.yaml`: the page configuration. Releases are assigned to categories by the names of their assets, so a release shows up under every component it ships a file for. Nextor 2 releases (tag `v2.*`) and anything published before 2026-09-01 are left out.
- `MAIN.md`: the content of the index page.
- `favicon.png`: the page icon.
- `generate.sh`: generates the page locally, see below (the published page is generated by a workflow).
- `build-pages.sh`: builds the whole Pages site locally, see below.
- `fake-releases.json`: fake releases data for trying configuration changes, see below.

## Regenerating the page

The page is regenerated automatically by the [Releases page workflow](../workflows/releases-page.yaml) whenever a release is published, edited, unpublished or deleted: it runs the generator (as a GitHub action) against the current releases and commits the updated `docs/releases` to `master`, which republishes the Pages site. A run in which nothing but the "Last update" timestamp of the page changes doesn't commit anything.

The workflow has to be run by hand (**Actions > Releases page > Run workflow**) after a change to `config.yaml` or `MAIN.md` reaches `master` (unless the regenerated page was committed along with it, see below), and in two cases where GitHub doesn't raise a release event that would trigger it:

- When the assets of a release are uploaded, deleted or renamed after the release is published. Since releases are categorized by their asset names, this matters; uploading the assets to a draft release and then publishing it is fine.
- When a release is edited whose tag points to a commit that doesn't contain the workflow (GitHub runs the version of the workflow present in the tagged commit), e.g. the releases published before the workflow was added.

To regenerate the page locally instead:

```
.github/categorized-releases/generate.sh
```

then open `docs/releases/index.html` in a browser to check the result. This is the way to check changes to `config.yaml` or `MAIN.md`; the regenerated page can be committed along with them, so that no manual run of the workflow is needed once they are merged. The script clones the generator into `bin/categorized-releases` on the first run (`bin/` is gitignored), at the exact version set in `generate.sh` so that the page comes out the same wherever it is regenerated; to move to a newer version of the generator, change the version there **and in the workflow** (they must match), then delete `bin/categorized-releases`. It needs Node.js 20 or later. The releases are read from the GitHub API; set `GITHUB_TOKEN` if the anonymous rate limit gets in the way.

## Trying configuration changes against fake releases

```
.github/categorized-releases/generate.sh --fake
```

generates the page from the releases described in `fake-releases.json` instead of the real ones, and writes it to `bin/releases-page` (open `bin/releases-page/index.html`), never to `docs/releases`, so that fake data can't be committed by accident. This is the way to try asset names or release layouts that don't exist yet.

`fake-releases.json` has the same format as the `--save-releases` output of the generator (a `repository` field plus a `releases` array, in descending publication date order); it can be rebuilt from the real releases with `node bin/categorized-releases/src/generate-release-page.js --repo Konamiman/Nextor --save-releases .github/categorized-releases/fake-releases.json`.

## Checking the whole Pages site locally

```
.github/categorized-releases/build-pages.sh
python3 -m http.server -d bin/pages-site 8000     # then open http://localhost:8000
```

This builds what GitHub Pages publishes: the `docs` directory rendered by Jekyll, releases page included. It runs the same container GitHub uses to build "deploy from a branch" sites (`ghcr.io/actions/jekyll-build-pages`), so the result is faithful, except that the site is built with an empty base URL so that it can be browsed from the root of a local web server (GitHub serves it under `/Nextor`). Requires Docker and a GitHub token (`GITHUB_TOKEN`, or a `gh` CLI login): the Jekyll metadata plugin insists on one, exactly as on GitHub.

## Publishing

For the site to be served, GitHub Pages must be enabled once by hand: **Settings > Pages > Source: Deploy from a branch**, branch `master`, folder `/docs`. From then on every push to the branch republishes the site, including the commits made by the releases page workflow. Jekyll processes the whole `docs` directory, so the Markdown documentation gets published as HTML pages too (`docs/_config.yml` holds the few Jekyll settings); the releases page is plain HTML and is copied as it is.
